permit_guide.1. Residential Building Permit (RBP): Required for new decks attached to a dwelling at any height; for free-standing decks more than 30 inches above grade at any point; for additions, porches with roofs, and structural alterations. Submittal: site plan, framing plan showing joist size and spacing, footing detail, ledger attachment detail (attached decks only), and contractor license number or owner-builder affidavit.
permit_guide.2. Minor Alteration Permit (MA): Non-structural interior work such as replacing cabinets, drywall under 200 sq ft, and like-for-like window replacement without enlarging openings. Not available for decks, porches or any exterior structure.
permit_guide.3. Exempt work: Free-standing decks not more than 30 inches above grade at any point, not serving a required exit door, and under 200 sq ft. Exempt work must still meet zoning setbacks. Replacement of an existing deck is treated the same as a new deck.
permit_guide.4. Zoning Clearance (ZC): Required in addition to any building permit when the structure is within 5 ft of a property line or in a historic overlay district.
permit_guide.5. Fees: Plan review fee is due at submittal; permit fee is due at issuance. RBP deck plan review: $185. Deck permit fee: $2.10 per sq ft. MA: flat $95.
permit_guide.6. Inspections: Footing, framing and final inspections are required for every RBP deck. Ledger flashing is checked at framing.
permit_guide.7. Guards: Guards are required where the walking surface is more than 30 inches above grade.

review_protocol.rule_on_integrity: Retracted publications are excluded (code R). Publications carrying an expression of concern are included provisionally, flagged, and re-checked before analysis; if later retracted they are excluded.
review_protocol.sensitivity_plan: A sensitivity analysis excluding trials with integrity flags will be reported.

record.title: Colchicine 0.5 mg daily after acute myocardial infarction: the COL-HEART randomised trial
record.abstract: Methods: 1,860 patients within 30 days of myocardial infarction were randomised to colchicine 0.5 mg daily or placebo. Primary outcome: composite of cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction and stroke. Results: Median follow-up 22 months. The primary outcome occurred less often with colchicine (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.84). Diarrhoea was more frequent with colchicine. Conclusions: Colchicine reduced ischaemic events after myocardial infarction.

notices.text: The editors have been made aware of concerns about the integrity of data from three of the 41 sites in the COL-HEART trial. An investigation by the sponsoring institution is under way. Readers should interpret the findings with caution until the investigation concludes.

Following the conclusion of the institutional investigation, the article is retracted. The investigation found that data from three sites, contributing approximately 14 percent of randomised patients, had been fabricated. The remaining authors were unable to provide a reanalysis acceptable to the journal. All authors except the investigator responsible for the three sites agreed to the retraction.

record.institution_statement: The sponsoring university confirmed that the investigation concluded that one site investigator fabricated follow-up visits and outcome data for patients at three sites under his supervision. No evidence of misconduct was found at the other 38 sites. The investigator has left the university. The university has notified the national research integrity office and the trial registry, and has offered the remaining site-level data to independent groups on request, subject to ethics approval.
record.registry_update: Registry record TR-58310 annotated: 'Primary publication retracted. See institutional statement.'
record.journal_statement: In a separate editorial, the journal explained that it considered publishing a corrected analysis limited to the 38 unaffected sites but decided against it because the trial's randomisation was stratified by site and the statistical analysis plan did not anticipate excluding sites; a post hoc subset would not carry the protections of the original design. The editors encouraged any group wishing to reanalyse the remaining data to register a new analysis plan first.

screening_history: Full-text screening: include, flagged for expression of concern, per rule_on_integrity.

payroll_tax_guide.T-1: Withholding follows the states where work is physically performed, unless a reciprocity agreement applies.
payroll_tax_guide.T-2: Easton-Westmark reciprocity: a resident of Westmark who works in Easton is taxed only by Westmark; the employee must file form REC-EW with payroll, after which payroll withholds Westmark tax only.
payroll_tax_guide.T-3: Until a REC-EW form is on file, payroll withholds for each state where work is performed, based on the approved work arrangement.
payroll_tax_guide.T-4: Remote days are sourced to the state of the employee's home address.
payroll_tax_guide.T-5: Employees are responsible for any state tax owed on filing; payroll corrects withholding prospectively once the setup is fixed.
payroll_tax_guide.T-6: Payroll Tax does not give individual tax advice; employees should consult a tax professional about prior-year filings.
payroll_tax_guide.T-7: State changes do not affect 401k deferral percentages or pre-tax commuter benefits.

state.payroll_faq: Reciprocity forms can be filed any time in self-service under Tax > State forms. Changes take effect on the next payroll after processing, and payroll does not refund prior withholding to one state because another state was owed.

state.memo_claim: Under the Carrin Water Act, utilities must test lead levels in every school annually (s. 12).

source.title: Carrin Water Act (consolidated)
source.excerpt:
s. 11 Definitions. 'Action level' means a lead concentration of 10 micrograms per litre in a first-draw sample. 'Facility' includes schools, childcare centres and residential care homes.

s. 12 Sampling in facilities. (1) A utility shall sample drinking water at each facility in its service area at least once every three years. (2) Where any sample at a facility exceeds the action level, the utility shall sample that facility annually until two consecutive annual samples are at or below the action level. (3) Results shall be sent to the facility operator within 30 days.

s. 13 Replacement of lead service lines. A utility shall maintain an inventory of lead service lines and replace no fewer than the prescribed number each year, prioritising lines serving facilities.

s. 14 Public reporting. Each utility shall publish an annual summary of sampling results by facility type.

s. 15 Offences. A utility that fails to comply with s. 12 commits an offence and is liable to a fine.

s. 16 Transitional. Facilities connected before the commencement of this Act shall be sampled for the first time within 18 months of commencement.

state.memo_context: Internal memo to school business managers, 'Water safety: what the Act requires of us'. Paragraph 2 contains the claim above. Paragraph 3 advises schools to keep the utility's sampling letters on file and to ask the utility for copies of any results above the action level. The memo's author is the district facilities lead; it has not been reviewed by legal counsel.
